title: Table Variables
description: Learn how to use table variables to hold rows of data in memory.

data.text: Table variables are variables that hold rows of data, similar to temporary tables. They are declared with the DECLARE statement.

data.title: Declare a table variable
data.content: Creates a table variable with three columns.

data.title: Insert and query a table variable
data.content: Inserts data and queries from a table variable.
data.code:
INSERT INTO @product_table
SELECT
    product_name,
    brand_id,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    category_id = 1;

SELECT * FROM @product_table;

items: Table variables cannot be altered after declaration.
They do not contain statistics — use for small datasets.
Cannot be used as input or output parameters.
Non-clustered indexes cannot be created on them (except memory-optimized in SQL Server 2014+).

data.title: Table Variables Key Points
points: Table variables are declared with DECLARE @name TABLE (...).
They have less locking overhead than temporary tables.
They are out of scope at the end of the batch.
Best for small datasets where statistics are not needed.
